title: ola-workflow project profile
description: Everything the workflow needs to know about one project. It lives either in ~/.claude/workflow-profiles/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/profile.json, which is yours and wins, or in <project>/.claude/workflow.json, which the project commits. Where the file lives says who owns it; the mode key below says how the workflow behaves. Any string value may hold {slot}, which `ola-profile get --slot N` replaces with the slot in use: that is how parallel agents get their own ports, databases and containers. Every glob here is a git pathspec `:(glob)`: no wildcard crosses a `/`, except `**`; a pattern with no slash is anchored at the repository root, unlike a .gitignore rule, so `Dockerfile*` takes only the one at the top and `**/Dockerfile*` every level; a directory named literally is recursive, so `docs` covers its subtree while `docs/*` covers one level, and no wildcard recurses that way, so `Dockerfile*` never reaches a neighbouring `Dockerfiles/`; and a leading `!` is not a negation but a pattern matching nothing, so an exclusion is written with the `exclude` key, never with a `!`. docs/configuration.md: Globs.

mode.description: integrated: the agents may write to the forge, and the coordinator may merge. discreet: memory stays local, no issue/label/status is ever written, push and PR creation need a human, and nothing is ever merged. Either value is legal in either location, though a committed profile is normally integrated and one you keep for someone else's repository is normally discreet.

github_tokens.description: keychain: every agent of a session works with the base GitHub token from the macOS keychain, which can neither merge nor write a commit status, and only the coordinator's exact merge command and the pr-reviewer's exact review-status command get a stronger one. GitHub refuses everything else with a 403, however it is spelled. off: the agents use the human's own GitHub login, with every right it has, and only the prompts keep merging and the review status with their roles. Defaults to keychain; the tokens are created with `ola-workflow-tokens setup`.

language.description: Languages to write in. Defaults to English everywhere.

human.description: What the coordinator says to the human.

base_branch.description: The branch PRs target and nobody may push to. Defaults to main.

check.description: How this project checks itself. These commands are the contract between the developers, the reviewer and CI.

affected.description: The subset for the current change.

cleanup.description: Run after a check to free containers, ports or volumes.

slots.description: How parallel agents avoid colliding on ports, databases and containers.

var.description: Environment variable carrying the slot. Defaults to SLOT.

developers.description: One slot per developer that may run at the same time.

reviewer.description: The slot, or slots, reserved for reviewers: one per review that may run at the same time.

pr.description: What a reviewable pull request looks like in this project.

max_lines.description: A PR above this must be split.

exclude.description: Globs that do not count towards max_lines (lockfiles, generated code).

merge.description: The merge gate the coordinator checks before merging, since a free GitHub plan has no ruleset to check it.

required_checks.description: Check names that must be successful on the head SHA.

review_status.description: Commit status context the reviewer sets, e.g. agent-review.

sensitive_paths.description: Globs no agent may merge: a human does it.

sensitive_patterns.description: A patch matching one of these needs a human, wherever it lands. Matching is per file: a match in a file the pattern applies to makes the patch sensitive, whatever else the patch touches. Otherwise touching one excluded test file would defuse the pattern, on the one key whose job is to force a human to look.

file.description: Glob the regex applies to. Omitted means every file.

regex.description: Perl-compatible regex matched against added lines.

exclude.description: Globs the pattern does not apply to, for files that mention the subject without touching it: tests, fixtures, documentation. It narrows `file` when both are given, so a file matching both is spared.

security.description: When a pull request gets a security review beside the code review.

paths.description: Globs whose change gets a security review: a pull request touching one of them is reviewed by the security-reviewer too. None declared, nobody is dispatched, and the pr-reviewer's checklist is the only security review.

commands.description: Declarative rules for project-specific commands. A command with allow_args is refused unless its arguments match; deny_args refuses only what matches.

cmd.description: First word of the command, e.g. eas, make, scalingo.

deny_args.description: Blacklist: only what matches is refused.

reason.description: Shown to the agent when the command is refused.

db_hosts_allowed.description: Database hosts an agent may connect to. Anything else is production until proven otherwise. A file-backed database (SQLite) has no host and is not covered: see issue #12.

context.description: Documents the agents read. Repository paths in integrated mode, paths inside the profile directory in discreet mode.

product.description: Users, personas, what counts as proven.

architecture.description: Layering, compatibility rules, how work is split.

review_checklist.description: Project-specific review rules, added to the base checklist.

security_precedents.description: What the security-reviewer does not report here, one precedent per false positive the human ruled on: the pattern, why it is not exploitable, and where it was ruled. Read from the base branch, never from the change under review. List it in merge.sensitive_paths too, so that only the human merges a new precedent.

design.description: Directory where each design is documented, one <slug>/ per design with its page and its README. Integrated mode only, default docs/design; in discreet mode designs stay in the profile's runs/<slug>/design/.

verify_ui.description: How a change is seen running, when looking at it is the only proof.

preview.description: How a web app is started to be photographed for a pull request: a URL that a headless browser captures. Not verify_ui, which is how a change is seen running by whoever develops it and may aim at a simulator; preview is web-only. `up` hands the shell back once the app answers at `url`: it does not stay in the foreground. `down` stops it, and a preview that cannot be stopped keeps its slot, so all three are required. {slot} applies to all three.

up.description: Starts the app and returns once it answers at `url`.

url.description: The address the app answers at, which `ola-workflow-capture` captures.

down.description: Stops the app and frees its slot.

escalation_extra.description: Subjects this project reserves for the human, on top of product, dependencies, process/security and release.
